blocks.title: Trigonometric Functions of Any Angle
content: Section 5.3. Reference angles, signs, exact values, and equations.

blocks.title: From an angle to a value
content: Locate the terminal side and its reference angle.
Use coordinates to explain a function’s sign.
Evaluate exact values and find every solution in an interval.
Optional extension: area from two sides and their included angle.

blocks.title: Which axis defines a reference angle?
content: For $\theta=150^\circ$, is the reference angle $30^\circ$ or $60^\circ$? Sketch your reason.
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.
answer: $30^\circ$: measure to the x-axis. The $60^\circ$ angle meets the y-axis.

blocks.title: The acute angle to the x-axis
content: The reference angle is the positive acute angle to the x-axis.
Reduce to $0\leq\theta<360^\circ$ first. In radians, replace $180^\circ$ by $\pi$ and $360^\circ$ by $2\pi$.
verification: Verify the signed coordinates, direction of rotation, and equal x/y scales in the attached SVG.

assets.alt: Equal-scale axes show a 150 degree counterclockwise angle in Quadrant II. The orange acute reference angle is measured from the negative x-axis to the terminal side, not from the y-axis.
assets.caption: Measure to the x-axis, even in Quadrant II.

blocks.title: Rotate, predict, then reveal
content: Choose an angle. Predict its reference angle and signs, then test your reasoning.
instructor_notes: Ask students to sketch 225 degrees before revealing. Compare -150 and 420 degrees. Finish at 90 degrees and ask why the acute-angle method stops applying.
Have a student choose the next preset and another student justify the result before revealing.

blocks.title: Different rotations, the same method
content: Find reference angles for $150^\circ$, $310^\circ$, $-120^\circ$, and $7\pi/4$.
verification: Verify the signed coordinates, direction of rotation, and equal x/y scales in the attached SVG.
steps: $-120^\circ$ is coterminal with $240^\circ$, so its reference angle is $60^\circ$.

assets.alt: Equal-scale axes show 150 degrees in Quadrant II, 310 degrees in Quadrant IV, negative 120 degrees ending in Quadrant III, and seven pi over four ending in Quadrant IV. The reference arcs meet the x-axis and no reference values are printed.

blocks.title: More than one full turn
content: Find the reference angle for 580°.
instructor_notes: Pause before revealing the solution.
verification: Verify the signed coordinates, direction of rotation, and equal x/y scales in the attached SVG.
answer: $580-360=220^\circ$, so the QIII reference angle is 40°.

assets.alt: A blue directed spiral turns counterclockwise 580 degrees and a teal terminal ray lies in Quadrant III. Equal-scale axes are shown. The requested reference angle is not labeled.
assets.caption: Remove full rotations before locating the reference angle.

blocks.title: A plausible angle, measured from the wrong axis
content: A student calls the orange $60^\circ$ angle the reference angle for $150^\circ$.
Explain the mistake to a partner, then state the correct reference angle.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.
verification: Verify the signed coordinates, direction of rotation, and equal x/y scales in the attached SVG.
answer: The orange arc meets the y-axis. The reference angle meets the x-axis: $180^\circ-150^\circ=30^\circ$.

assets.alt: Equal-scale axes show a 150 degree terminal side in Quadrant II. An orange 60 degree arc runs from the positive y-axis to the terminal side and is labeled with a question mark. Students must explain why measuring from the y-axis does not give the reference angle.

content: State the quadrant formulas for reference angles.

blocks.title: Two sign clues, one quadrant
content: If tangent is positive and cosine is negative, which quadrant is possible?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.
answer: Quadrant III. Both sign conditions must hold at the same time.

blocks.title: Coordinates explain the signs
content: ASTC summarizes positive functions by quadrant.
Signs follow from x, y, and positive r.
verification: Verify the signed coordinates, direction of rotation, and equal x/y scales in the attached SVG.

assets.alt: A unit circle on equal-scale axes shows positive x and y in Quadrant I, negative x and positive y in II, negative x and y in III, and positive x and negative y in IV. Radius r is positive everywhere.
assets.caption: The signs come from x and y; r is always positive.

blocks.title: Intersect the possible quadrants
content: Determine the quadrant if $\tan\theta>0$ and $\cos\theta<0$.
steps: Tangent is positive in Quadrants I and III.
Cosine is negative in Quadrants II and III.

blocks.title: Choose a quadrant and defend it
content: Determine the quadrant if $\sin\theta>0$ and $\sec\theta<0$.
instructor_notes: Pause before revealing the solution.

blocks.title: Check the coordinate signs
content: Use the intersection of sign conditions.
Reciprocal functions share the sign of their partner.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.

blocks.title: Explain a sign without the mnemonic
content: Explain ASTC using the signs of x and y rather than memorization.

blocks.title: What stays positive?
content: What does r represent for a point $(x,y)$ on a terminal side?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: Six ratios from one terminal point
content: For a nonzero terminal point $(x,y)$, $r=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}>0$.
$\sin\theta=y/r$, $\cos\theta=x/r$, $\tan\theta=y/x$.
$\csc\theta=r/y$, $\sec\theta=r/x$, $\cot\theta=x/y$.
A function is undefined when its denominator is zero.

blocks.title: Angles on the coordinate axes
content: At $90^\circ$, $x=0$: $\sin\theta=1$, $\cos\theta=0$, and $\tan\theta$ is undefined.
At $180^\circ$, $y=0$: $\sin\theta=0$, $\cos\theta=-1$, and $\cot\theta$ is undefined.
These angles have no acute reference angle. Check the denominator directly.

assets.alt: Two equal-scale unit circles show the point (0,1) at 90 degrees and the point (-1,0) at 180 degrees. At 90 degrees x is zero; at 180 degrees y is zero. No acute reference angle is drawn.
assets.caption: An axis point can put zero in a denominator.

verification: Verify the signed coordinates, direction of rotation, and equal x/y scales in the attached SVG.

blocks.title: Identities and possible values
content: $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$; $\tan\theta=\sin\theta/\cos\theta$ where defined.
$\csc\theta=1/\sin\theta$, $\sec\theta=1/\cos\theta$, $\cot\theta=\cos\theta/\sin\theta$ where defined.
$-1\leq\sin\theta\leq1$ and $-1\leq\cos\theta\leq1$.
Use the quadrant to choose the sign after taking a square root.

blocks.title: A point in Quadrant II
content: For $P=(-3,4)$, calculate r and all six trigonometric values.
verification: Verify exact values and quadrant signs.
Verify the signed coordinates, direction of rotation, and equal x/y scales in the attached SVG.

assets.alt: An equal-scale coordinate diagram plots P=(-3,4). The horizontal directed coordinate is -3, the vertical directed coordinate is 4, and the radial length is labeled r without revealing its value. The blue angle is measured counterclockwise from positive x.
assets.caption: The signed coordinates locate the point. The radius is a length.

blocks.title: Distance and coordinates have different roles
content: r is always positive.
Rationalize denominators only when required by course convention.

content: Describe the point-to-ratios workflow in three steps.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: solve a sine or cosine equation
content: Find all $\theta$ in $[0^\circ,360^\circ)$ with $\sin\theta=-\tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}$.
steps: Sine is negative in Quadrants III and IV.
instructor_notes: Quiz 10 has one sine and one cosine equation of this kind; stress that there are two answers on one rotation.
Retained from the November 9 lesson as an optional exact-equation example.
verification: Verify sin 225° = sin 315° = −√2/2.
Check the labeled geometry and accessibility text of solve-sine.svg.

assets.alt: A unit circle with a dashed horizontal line at y equals negative root 2 over 2. It crosses the circle at two points, on terminal sides at 225 degrees in Quadrant III and 315 degrees in Quadrant IV. Each makes a 45 degree reference angle with the x-axis.
assets.caption: Two terminal sides meet the line y = −√2/2.

blocks.title: You Try: solve a cosine equation
content: Find all $\theta$ in $[0^\circ,360^\circ)$ with $\cos\theta=-\tfrac{\sqrt2}{2}$.
answer: Reference angle $45^\circ$; cosine is negative in Quadrants II and III, so $\theta=135^\circ$ and $\theta=225^\circ$.
verification: Verify cos 135° = cos 225° = −√2/2.
instructor_notes: Students should name the quadrants before computing.
Retained from the November 9 lesson as an optional exact-equation example.

blocks.title: Calculator output and interval solutions
content: Find all solutions of $\sin\theta=-0.848$ with $0^\circ\leq\theta<360^\circ$. Round to two decimals.
steps: $\arcsin(-0.848)\approx-57.99^\circ$ points to QIV, but lies outside the interval.
Use the unrounded $\alpha\approx57.994800^\circ$. Sine is negative in QIII and QIV.
$\theta=360^\circ-\alpha\approx302.01^\circ$. Check both points on the circle.

assets.alt: A unit circle on equal-scale axes intersects the horizontal line y=-0.848 twice, in Quadrants III and IV. Teal rays reach both intersections. A blue clockwise arc marks the negative principal inverse-sine output at the Quadrant IV ray. No final solution angles are printed.
assets.caption: Both intersections satisfy the same sine equation.

verification: Verify the signed coordinates, direction of rotation, and equal x/y scales in the attached SVG.

blocks.title: All solutions, including no solution
content: Find all solutions on $0^\circ\leq\theta<360^\circ$, rounded to two decimals.
answer: (c) No real solution: a sine value must lie in $[-1,1]$.
instructor_notes: Keep full calculator precision until the final answers. Ask students to justify the quadrants.

blocks.title: Can an equation have no angles?
content: A student writes two angles for $\sin\theta=-1.637$.
Name a check that would catch the error before using a calculator.
answer: No real angle has that sine value. A calculator domain error is expected.

blocks.title: Exit check
content: Individually: find all solutions of $\cos\theta=-0.75$ on $0^\circ\leq\theta<360^\circ$.
Sketch both terminal sides and explain why a principal output alone can miss a solution.
answer: Every final angle must satisfy both the equation and the stated interval.
